AcceptRead.description:
The accept's whole answer: the entity born, and the proposed relations
that could not be placed. The skips are transient — the response carries
them once (D8), the UI announces them, nothing persists them.
AcceptRead.title: AcceptRead

ActivityPoint.description:
One day of the activity window: the date and the atelier's net words.

The net is honest — a day that removed more text than it added carries
a negative count, and a day without a row carries zero.
ActivityPoint.title: ActivityPoint

ActivityRead.description:
The atelier's activity across all the user's novels (W3).

``points`` cover the requested window oldest-first, zero-days
included; ``streak_days`` counts consecutive days with a nonzero net
ending today — or yesterday, which keeps the streak alive until the
day after tomorrow without writing; ``weekly_average`` is the mean
net words per day over ALL days of the window (zero-days in the
basis), one decimal; ``today_words`` is today's net across novels.

The daily goal (W4 row 25) is the user's own ``daily_goal_words`` —
atelier scope, never a book target; ``None`` is the honest unset.
``goal_met`` is true exactly when a goal is stored and today's net
reaches it; ``goal_remaining`` is what the day still owes,
``max(0, goal - today_words)`` — a negative day owes the goal plus
the removal — and 0 when no goal is stored or the day is done.
ActivityRead.title: ActivityRead

ArchiveInvalidRead.description: The 422 detail when the archive itself is unreadable or malformed.
ArchiveInvalidRead.title: ArchiveInvalidRead

AssignmentRead.description:
A stored assignment as every read shows it: the model and the profile.

The profile fields mirror the row's columns — ``custom`` beside its
number, the vocabulary's default where no choice was stored.
AssignmentRead.title: AssignmentRead

AssignmentUpdate.description:
``profile_id: null`` clears the task's assignment (back down the cascade).

``output_profile`` is the task's output-length choice (W8): a vocabulary
name (:data:`OUTPUT_PROFILES`) or an explicit number — the number *is*
the custom profile's carrier, there is no ``"custom"`` string. Absent
and carried null both mean ``balanced``: the profile column has no
two-state semantics, so a save that omits the field states ``balanced``
by that fact. A custom number above the assigned model's stored
``max_output_tokens`` is refused by the service's gate (422 naming the
field); with no stored ceiling nothing bounds it.
AssignmentUpdate.title: AssignmentUpdate

ChapterOrderUpdate.description:
The PUT chapter-order body: the whole rail, in its new order.

Every chapter of the novel and nothing else — an arrangement is a
permutation of the ids the book holds this moment, so the service
compares the body against the stored set as one whole and refuses a
stale one (a second tab's add, delete or repeat) with the current
order, rather than reshape what the writer no longer sees.
ChapterOrderUpdate.title: ChapterOrderUpdate

ConflictRead.description:
One item the merge rules refused: which archive file, and why.

`file` carries the archive-side path the parse stamped on the item —
untrusted text, a plain string by contract. `code` is the stable key the
receipt localizes, with `params` interpolated; `reason` is the technical
detail, and the fallback for a code the client does not know.
ConflictRead.title: ConflictRead

ConsistencyAccepted.description: The check's enqueue answer: what to poll.
ConsistencyAccepted.title: ConsistencyAccepted

DriverRead.description:
The instance's driver kind as one word: what actually answers.

``fake`` while every assignable task's serving tier is the local fake
adapter — the cascade's floor or a stored fake row; ``configured`` once
any provider adapter serves one. The offline card claims a local driver
only on ``fake``. The read is the tasks read's own resolution reduced to
this word, never a second derivation, so it can never disagree with the
task list's rows — and it fails as the tasks read fails: a provider
whose key its tier can no longer produce is the 502 the router maps.
DriverRead.title: DriverRead

EmbeddingMismatchDetail.description: Identify incompatible stored and current embedding widths.
EmbeddingMismatchDetail.title: EmbeddingMismatchDetail

EmbeddingMismatchRead.description: The HTTP 409 body returned when source embeddings are incompatible.
EmbeddingMismatchRead.title: EmbeddingMismatchRead

EntityCreate.description:
The POST body of an entity: its fields and the relation lines to place.

The values are checked by the service against the same contract the
update path reads — the schema only carries them, so a refusal is the
coded ``entity-invalid``, never the framework's field list.
EntityCreate.title: EntityCreate

EntityMerge.description: The merge's whole ask: which row survives.
EntityMerge.title: EntityMerge

EntityUpdate.description:
The PATCH body: only the fields present are the change.

``None`` is ambiguous by shape alone — an absent field and a cleared
content both look like None — so the service reads
``model_fields_set`` to tell a carried change from a missing one. The
values are checked there, against the parse contract's vocabulary and
the label rules: this schema carries the fields, the contract decides
what a value may be. A carried ``null`` content clears the body.
EntityUpdate.title: EntityUpdate

ExportDone.description: The receipt of a path export: where it went and how much.
ExportDone.title: ExportDone

ExportRequest.description: One export: into a directory on disk, or as a ZIP download.
ExportRequest.title: ExportRequest

ExtractionAccepted.description: The enqueue's whole answer: what to poll.
ExtractionAccepted.title: ExtractionAccepted

ExtractionRequest.description: Which chapter of the novel the worker should read.
ExtractionRequest.title: ExtractionRequest

FieldRefusalRead.description: One refused field inside a 422 body — `loc` names the request part.
FieldRefusalRead.title: FieldRefusalRead

FieldRefusalsRead.description: The 422 body when the request breaks a field contract.
FieldRefusalsRead.title: FieldRefusalsRead

ImportRefusalsRead.description: The import's 422 body: a refused field, or the offending archive file.
ImportRefusalsRead.title: ImportRefusalsRead

ImportReportRead.description:
What one import did, per class — the engine's report, field by field.

Every matched item lands in exactly one of new / revised / renamed /
already_current; an item a conflict refused increments nothing.
ImportReportRead.title: ImportReportRead

JobRead.description: What a UI polls: the row's state, not its payload.
JobRead.title: JobRead

ModelCreate.description:
One new model under one of the user's providers.

The provider is named, not repeated: kind, endpoint and key live there.
The service's gate refuses a ``provider_id`` that is not the user's —
the schema cannot know ownership, only shape.
ModelCreate.title: ModelCreate

ModelRead.description:
A model as every read shows it: its provider named, no key anywhere.

The key and its mask live on the provider; the model carries none. The
four state fields are the settings row's marks, read-only facts:
``in_catalog`` is the resolution lookup's own answer (:func:`effective_info`
with the provider's vendor — no second lookup path), and the
``last_error_*`` pair is the model's newest audit row, kept only when that
call failed, so a later success clears the mark. ``catalog_max_output_tokens``
is that same lookup's own output ceiling for the model string — beside,
never merged into, the model's stored ``max_output_tokens``, whose column
keeps its own meaning (the one ceiling a custom choice is bounded by).
ModelRead.title: ModelRead

ModelTestResult.description: What one connection test found: it ran, and it either answered or named why.
ModelTestResult.title: ModelTestResult

ModelUpdate.description:
What a patch may change. The provider and the model string can move.

Absent fields stay unchanged; present nulls clear the tunables. Clearing
the name, the provider or the model string is refused by the service —
a model without one of them is not a configuration. ``is_default: true``
hands the default over from the current holder.
ModelUpdate.title: ModelUpdate

NovelUpdate.description:
The PATCH body: only the fields present are the change.

``None`` is ambiguous by shape alone — an absent field and a cleared
author both look like None — so the service reads
``model_fields_set`` to tell a carried change from a missing one. The
values are checked there, against the novel contract's trims and
limits: this schema carries the fields, the contract decides what a
value may be. A carried ``null`` clears author, genre, blurb or
language; the title is never clearable.

The shelf's fields (W3) ride the same rule: ``status`` answers to the
vocabulary (draft|revision|final) at the service boundary,
``series_id`` must name a series the user owns, ``series_volume`` is
a positive number that needs a series link, and ``archived_at`` is a
timestamp — carrying one archives the book, carrying ``null``
unarchives it.

The wizard's per-novel answers (W4 §5) ride it too: ``target_words``
and the four setup settings — typology, dramatic form, AI role, canon
strictness — are checked at the service boundary against the kernel
contract's shared vocabularies and bounds, the same constants setup's
request validates against. A carried ``null`` clears the answer back
to the honest unset; the book-settings dialog edits what setup bound.
NovelUpdate.title: NovelUpdate

OrderMismatchRead.description: The 409 body for a chapter-order mismatch: the stored ids in position order.
OrderMismatchRead.title: OrderMismatchRead

PlanningErrorRead.description: The JSON body for a missing chapter aggregate or a refused PUT.
PlanningErrorRead.title: PlanningErrorRead

PresetRead.description:
One provider preset as the create form reads it, with the catalog join.

The preset is the kernel table's row — label, model and vendor are the
vendors' proper spellings, data rather than catalog text. ``models`` is
the vendor's catalog vocabulary, bare and sorted, the model picker's
list; a vendor the catalog does not carry joins to an empty list and the
form still saves free text. ``snapshot_date`` is the catalog's own date,
``None`` when the snapshot names none — the picker's honesty mark rides
this response, so the form needs no second call.
PresetRead.title: PresetRead

PromptCodedDetail.description:
The live test's coded face: the code the surfaces localize, the detail
behind it — the chat frames' vocabulary, one spelling for both routers.
PromptCodedDetail.title: PromptCodedDetail

PromptCodedError.description: The live test's HTTP faces (409, 429, 502, 503): the coded detail body.
PromptCodedError.title: PromptCodedError

PromptDetail.description:
One key as the editor shows it: the bundled source, the variable
legend, the override in force, the source a render would use.
PromptDetail.title: PromptDetail

PromptDiff.description: The bundled template against the override in force for the scope.
PromptDiff.title: PromptDiff

PromptKeyNotFound.description: The 404 body: no bundled prompt carries the key.
PromptKeyNotFound.title: PromptKeyNotFound

PromptLiveTestBody.description:
The live test's body: the editor draft (absent = the saved effective)
and the scope. An absent body altogether tests the saved effective too.
PromptLiveTestBody.title: PromptLiveTestBody

PromptOverride.description: The override in force for the scope: which tier answered, its content.
PromptOverride.title: PromptOverride

PromptPreview.description: The editor's preview: the rendered text, the provenance, the diagnostics.
PromptPreview.title: PromptPreview

PromptPreviewBody.description:
The preview's optional body: the editor draft to render.

Absent (or carrying no ``content``) previews the saved effective source.
``novel_id`` rides the query string, beside the other reads; the body is
the POST's optional draft — a browser's ``fetch`` refuses a GET body, so
the render computation posts.
PromptPreviewBody.title: PromptPreviewBody

PromptPreviewDiagnostics.description:
What the render found beyond the text: its size and the contract's verdict.

``contract_ok`` is ``None`` for a key without a contract, ``False`` for a
draft that renders but would fail its key's save-time gate — the preview
shows both facts, the refusal stays the save's.
PromptPreviewDiagnostics.title: PromptPreviewDiagnostics

PromptRefusal.description: The save gate's 422 body: which rule refused, and what it said.
PromptRefusal.title: PromptRefusal

PromptSave.description: One override write. ``novel_id`` absent or null saves the global tier.
PromptSave.title: PromptSave

PromptSummary.description:
One bundled key in the list, with its two override tiers as facts.

``override_novel`` is meaningful only when the read carried a
``novel_id``; without one there is no novel tier to ask.
PromptSummary.title: PromptSummary

PromptVariable.description: One variable of the template, with the sample value as its example.
PromptVariable.title: PromptVariable

PromptVariableProvenance.description:
One declared variable: its sample value, and whether the source reads it.

``used`` is the AST's own verdict — a load context in the parsed source —
so a variable the source names inside a comment-style construct counts
as little as the render itself counts it.
PromptVariableProvenance.title: PromptVariableProvenance

Proposal.description: The dialog's draft: the slot set, its marks and the proposed relations.
Proposal.title: Proposal

ProposedRelation.description: One proposed relation, with the provenance the server decided.
ProposedRelation.title: ProposedRelation

ProposedRelationRead.description:
One proposed relation as review reads it: the target's name and the type.

The stored proposals speak the extraction answer's keys (``target``,
``type``); the read shape names them target_name and relation_type, and
both spellings validate.
ProposedRelationRead.title: ProposedRelationRead

ProviderCreate.description:
One new provider: the saved endpoint its models hang off.

``api_key`` is write-only; the mask comes back.
ProviderCreate.title: ProviderCreate

ProviderCreated.description:
The create's answer: the one response that carries the full key.

``api_key`` is the plaintext exactly once, for the client that just sent
it to confirm against; it is ``None`` when no key was stored (a fake, or
a local endpoint without one).
ProviderCreated.title: ProviderCreated

ProviderRead.description: A provider as every read shows it: the mask, never the key.
ProviderRead.title: ProviderRead

ProviderUpdate.description:
What a patch may change. The kind is what the provider is: not editable.

Absent fields stay unchanged; present nulls clear the nullable columns.
ProviderUpdate.title: ProviderUpdate

ReembedResult.description:
What a re-embed rebuilt: every document and every chunk of it — the
corpus ends at one width again.
ReembedResult.title: ReembedResult

RelationCreate.description:
The POST body of an edge: the other end, a free-text type, a note.

The type is free text on purpose (D7) — the suggested vocabulary is a
UI autocomplete, not an API constraint; the service checks blankness
and length, and the refusal is the coded ``entity-invalid`` the create
endpoint speaks, never the framework's field list. The ends are taken
from the path and this body and are immutable afterwards.
RelationCreate.title: RelationCreate

RelationLine.description:
One relation line of a create-by-hand body: the target row, its type,
an optional note. The client resolved the target to an entity id before
the request; the service still checks the row belongs to the novel.

The type carries no schema bounds: a blank or over-long label is the
service's ``entity-invalid`` refusal (coded, naming the field), not the
framework's field list.
RelationLine.title: RelationLine

RelationPatch.description:
The PATCH body of an edge: type and note only.

The ends are immutable — moving an edge is delete plus create — so no
field here could carry them. ``model_fields_set`` tells a carried
``null`` note (cleared) from an absent one (untouched). The type carries
no schema bounds: a blank or over-long label is the service's coded
``entity-invalid``, the create endpoint's own answer.
RelationPatch.title: RelationPatch

RemapEntry.description:
One chapter's move: the stage it stands in now, and the one the
target structure suggests.
RemapEntry.title: RemapEntry

RemapRead.description:
The remap answer: the target structure, whether it was applied, and
the per-chapter mapping — preview and confirm agree chapter by chapter.
RemapRead.title: RemapRead

RemapRequest.description:
The remap body: the target structure, and whether to apply it.

``confirm: false`` previews the mapping without writing a row;
``confirm: true`` writes the assignments plus the novel setting in one
transaction — exactly the previewed mapping.
RemapRequest.title: RemapRequest

SceneAggregateRead.description:
The chapter's scenes in position order, with the version the dock
compares its snapshot against: the chapter's own stamp, touched by
every aggregate write.
SceneAggregateRead.title: SceneAggregateRead

SceneAggregateUpdate.description: The PUT body: the chapter's whole scene list, in its new order.
SceneAggregateUpdate.title: SceneAggregateUpdate

SceneContinue.description:
The continue body (W4 D5): the writer's optional instruction.

An absent body, an empty object and a carried ``null`` are one behavior —
today's continuation, no instruction. The bound is the chat question's own
(``ChatRequest.question``: 1-2000 characters of the raw string, no trim):
the schema's one refusal, a 422 naming the field before any stream starts.
What the window cannot hold beside the scaffold is the builder's refusal,
the coded budget frame — never a truncated instruction.
SceneContinue.title: SceneContinue

SceneOrderMismatchRead.description: The 409 body for a scene-order mismatch: the stored ids in position order.
SceneOrderMismatchRead.title: SceneOrderMismatchRead

SceneOrderUpdate.description:
The PUT scene-order body: the whole chapter, in its new order.

Every scene of the chapter and nothing else — an arrangement is a
permutation of the ids the chapter holds this moment, so the service
compares the body against the stored set as one whole and refuses a
stale one (a second tab's add, delete or repeat) with the current
order, rather than reshape what the writer no longer sees.
SceneOrderUpdate.title: SceneOrderUpdate

SceneUpdate.description:
The PUT scene body: only the fields present are the change.

Title and body keep the chapter's rule — ``None`` is unchanged, ``""``
after the service's trim is the honest empty (the title's placeholder a
rendering, the body emptied). The two labels are present-and-nullable
like the novel's metadata: an absent field is no change, a carried
``null`` clears the label back to the honest unset. The service reads
``model_fields_set`` to tell a carried change from a missing one; the
lengths are the schema's one refusal.
SceneUpdate.title: SceneUpdate

SceneUpsert.description:
One scene of the PUT aggregate, by stable id.

New scenes carry client-generated ids — the diff treats an id the
chapter does not know and nobody else owns as a creation. The body
carries no timestamps: those are the server's own.
SceneUpsert.title: SceneUpsert

SeriesCreate.description:
One new series: the name the shelf groups its volumes by. The width
is a novel title's own (the column's String(200)); the service trims
and refuses a whitespace-only name — a series is named like a book.
SeriesCreate.title: SeriesCreate

SessionCreate.description: The door's request: one novel, one mode, and the type the panel fixed.
SessionCreate.title: SessionCreate

SessionDetail.description: The session with its transcript, up to the read limit, oldest first.
SessionDetail.title: SessionDetail

SessionList.description:
The novel's interviews: open first, then closed, newest first in each state.

Up to ``SESSION_LIST_LIMIT`` in each state.
SessionList.title: SessionList

SessionRead.description: One interview as every read shows it.
SessionRead.title: SessionRead

SessionSummary.description:
One row of the novel's session list: identity, type and the draft's name.

The list renders a header and a state per session, so it carries no
proposal — opening the session reads the transcript and the draft.
SessionSummary.title: SessionSummary

SetupResult.description:
The provisioning facts step 4 and the landing render.

``genre`` is the effective genre — the archive's own on the demo path,
the passed genre on the blank path — and ``chapters`` the count the
import/creation produced. The settings are nullable as the model is:
a novel without an answer does not lie.
SetupResult.title: SetupResult

SkippedRelationRead.description:
A proposed relation accept could not place: the target's name as the
proposal spelled it, the type as accept stores it — the stripped form
a hand-added edge would carry, not the proposal's raw words.
SkippedRelationRead.title: SkippedRelationRead

StageAssignmentUpdate.description:
The PUT body: the chapter's new stage, a key of the current structure.
The body carries no timestamps: those are the server's own.
StageAssignmentUpdate.title: StageAssignmentUpdate

StoryboardChapterRead.description:
One chapter in its storyboard column: the effective stage, where the
stage came from, and how closely the writing follows the plan.

``assignment_source`` is ``assigned`` when the writer set the stage by
hand, ``suggested`` when the column is the position-ratio suggestion —
a suggestion is computed, never persisted. ``sync_status`` is one of
``empty | planned | deviated | completed | on_track``.
StoryboardChapterRead.title: StoryboardChapterRead

StoryboardRead.description: The novel's whole storyboard: the structure and its staged chapters.
StoryboardRead.title: StoryboardRead

StoryboardStageRead.description: One storyboard column with the chapters standing in it.
StoryboardStageRead.title: StoryboardStageRead

SuggestedParts.description:
Which slot values the model proposed rather than the writer.

A list slot carries its provenance per item: the values that are suggested.
SuggestedParts.title: SuggestedParts

TaskEffectiveRead.description:
One known task key and the tier that actually serves it.

``profile_id`` and ``profile_name`` are ``None`` exactly when no model
serves — the environment tier answers. ``kind`` names the serving adapter
either way (``fake``, ``openai-chat`` or ``anthropic``), so the page can
say what answers without claiming the cascade's stored choice. An
audit-only key has no serving tier: ``kind`` is ``audit``, the model
fields are ``None``, and ``assignable`` is ``False``.

The output profile is the honesty seam (W8): ``output_profile`` names the
choice the serving assignment carried (``balanced`` when none did) and
``resolved_output_tokens`` is the number a call reserves — the target,
``min``-ed with the model's stored ``max_output_tokens`` where one is
stored, the target itself where none is (an unknown ceiling is never
invented). An audit-only key names no profile and reserves nothing:
both fields are ``None`` there.
TaskEffectiveRead.title: TaskEffectiveRead

TimelineEventCreate.description:
The POST body: one event on the novel's timeline.

The body carries no timestamps: those are the server's own. ``position``
is the manual order (null leaves the event unordered, listed last);
``date_label`` is the optional free-text date; ``character_names`` are
free-text names for now — no KB linkage in this slice.
TimelineEventCreate.title: TimelineEventCreate

TimelineEventUpdate.description:
The PUT body: only the fields present are the change.

A carried ``null`` clears ``chapter_id`` or ``position``; an absent
field leaves it alone. Every other field is non-nullable — a carried
null is a 422 at the boundary, never a NOT NULL violation on write.
A blank title is refused, never stored.
TimelineEventUpdate.title: TimelineEventUpdate

TurnCreate.description:
One writer turn: what the panel sent, and the choice it named.

``text`` may be empty only for ``accept-suggestion``: there the server
stores the settled suggestion's own text, never the client's words.
TurnCreate.title: TurnCreate

TurnRead.description: One transcript line and its suggestion state.
TurnRead.title: TurnRead

TurnReadback.description: What one turn answered: the reply, the merged proposal, the suggestion.
TurnReadback.title: TurnReadback

UpdateDismiss.description:
The version the reader asked to ignore; a newer one announces again.

Widths are the columns': the tag is at most 64 characters, so an over-long
value is the gate's 422, never a Postgres error at the write.
UpdateDismiss.title: UpdateDismiss

UpdateRead.description:
The answer the shell renders: the version, the last known release, and
whether that release is still worth announcing.

``latest_version``, the notes and the link are the last known release, so
an offline instance still shows what it heard before. ``update_available``
is computed on the server — newer than the running version and not the
dismissed one — and ``dismissed`` names the banner the reader asked to stop.
UpdateRead.title: UpdateRead

ValidationBody.description:
The framework's own 422 body, mirrored for the union beside the
refusal — FastAPI builds its schema from a dict, so nothing imports.
ValidationBody.title: ValidationBody

ValidationItem.description:
One of the framework's request-validation failures, mirrored so the
documented 422 union covers both bodies a route can answer with.
ValidationItem.title: ValidationItem

WritingErrorRead.description: The JSON body for missing resources and incomplete setup.
WritingErrorRead.title: WritingErrorRead

post.description: Stream a sourced answer; return HTTP 409 for incompatible source embeddings.

text/event-stream.description: Server-sent events: data frames for the sources and the answer, then one terminal event: done or error.

get.description:
The novel's interviews for this user, open first then closed, newest first per state.

Up to ``SESSION_LIST_LIMIT`` per state.

post.description: Open an interview: mode, type, novel and any target decide; a coded 404 or 422.

get.description: The session with its transcript, up to ``TRANSCRIPT_READ_LIMIT`` turns, oldest first.

post.description: End the interview; closing an already closed session answers it unchanged.
Take one turn; the refusal names why nothing (or only the marks) moved.

get.description: Return an owned job's state; absent and other users' jobs both raise HTTP 404.

schema.title: Response List Documents Api Knowledge Documents Get

post.description: Ingest a text file. Plain text only; the body is decoded as UTF-8.

delete.description:
Delete a document. Its chunks' foreign key cascades: the passages go
with the row, and search cannot find its text again.

Raise HTTP 404 for an absent or unowned document.

post.description:
Create an entity by hand, with its relation lines, in one transaction.

Return the entity; raise HTTP 404 for an absent or unowned novel, or
HTTP 422 for an invalid name, type or label (``entity-invalid``), more
than twelve relation lines (``relation-limit``), a relation line outside
the novel (``relation-target-invalid``, naming the row), or a duplicate
line (``relation-duplicate``).

delete.description:
Delete an entity. Its relations' foreign keys cascade: the edges go
with the row.

Raise HTTP 404 for an absent or unowned entity.

patch.description:
Correct an entity by hand: only the fields the body carries change.

Return the entity; raise HTTP 404 for an absent or unowned entity, or
HTTP 422 for an invalid name, type, alias or tag — a null content
clears the body.

post.description:
Fold this entity into another: the target survives, the source is
deleted, and the source's edges re-point and its fields fold into the
survivor.

Return the folded target; raise HTTP 404 if either entity is absent or
unowned, or HTTP 422 for a self-merge or a target in another novel.

get.description:
The entity's relations, both directions, oldest first.

Raise HTTP 404 for an absent or unowned entity — another user's rows
are the same absence, including their edges.

schema.title: Response List Relations Api Knowledge Entities  Entity Id  Relations Get

post.description:
Create a directed edge to another entity of the same novel.

Self-relations are allowed. Raise HTTP 404 when either end is absent
or unowned or not of this novel, HTTP 422 for a blank or over-long
type (``entity-invalid``, the create endpoint's own shape), or HTTP 409
when this exact edge carries the type already.

Enqueue entity extraction for a chapter. The worker does the rest; poll
``GET /api/jobs/{job_id}`` — the row's state is the answer.

Respond with HTTP 404 for an absent or unowned novel or chapter, including
a chapter from a different novel, or HTTP 409 when setup is required.

Acknowledge: the finding is consumed — seen, the text stays as it is.

Return the finding; raise HTTP 404 for an absent or unowned finding,
or HTTP 409 for an already reviewed finding.

Dismiss a finding and return its retained row with status dismissed.

Raise HTTP 404 for an absent or unowned finding, or HTTP 409 if already reviewed.

get.description:
The novel's entities: filtered by type and tag, or fuzzy-found by q
(the trigram tier); unfiltered, oldest first.

Raise HTTP 404 for an absent or unowned novel.

schema.title: Response List Entities Api Knowledge Novels  Novel Id  Entities Get

get.description:
The novel's findings in one review state; pending is the queue.

Return them oldest first; raise HTTP 404 for an absent or unowned novel.

schema.title: Response List Findings Api Knowledge Novels  Novel Id  Findings Get

get.description:
The novel's whole relation set, oldest first — the graph canvas's one
read call instead of a per-entity fan-out.

Raise HTTP 404 for an absent or unowned novel.

schema.title: Response List Novel Relations Api Knowledge Novels  Novel Id  Relations Get

get.description:
The novel's suggestions in one review state; pending is the queue.

Return them oldest first; raise HTTP 404 for an absent or unowned novel.

schema.title: Response List Suggestions Api Knowledge Novels  Novel Id  Suggestions Get

post.description: Re-embed the corpus through the configured model: the mismatch fix.

delete.description:
Delete one edge: exactly the edge.

Raise HTTP 404 for an absent or unowned edge.

patch.description:
Retype or re-note an edge; the ends are immutable.

Return the edge; raise HTTP 404 for an absent or unowned edge,
HTTP 422 for a blank or over-long type (``entity-invalid``, the create
endpoint's own shape), or HTTP 409 when the new type would duplicate the
edge's sibling.
